texts: bad: 'leave the tide-pools dry' is a result-state clause whose object is a definite plural, sitting inside a generic claim about neap tides — so the parse had to bury the half that hands 'dry' to each individual pool inside the generic rule's own conclusion, where its variable is bound by nothing and it carries no truth value of its own. No placement of that half is licensed (at the top level it would assert every tide-pool dry unconditionally), so as parsed the dryness of any one pool never actually derives. Rewrite it as a property that holds under a stated condition: "Tide-pools are dry at neap tide." That is a single licensed atom — the property 'dry' on the tide-pool kind, with 'neap tide' as the condition — which the reasoner can hand to any pool during a neap tide; the only shift is that the pools are the kind rather than one definite set, and the tide is named as the condition instead of the grammatical subject.
